For Re s>1 Euler's product, absolute convergence, and Stieltjes integration give
[
 -\zeta'/\zeta(s)
   ={s\over s-1}+s\int_1^\infty (\psi(t)-t)t^{-s-1}dt.
]
The integral up to e^200 is entire and the remaining integral is locally
normally convergent for Re s>27/32 under D02. For example on a compact set
with Re s >= 27/32+epsilon, its integrand is dominated by a constant times
t^(-1-epsilon) (log t)^2. By uniqueness of meromorphic continuation, the
log derivative has no pole in this open half-plane other than s=1. A
zero of any positive multiplicity would give a pole there. Thus D02
implies Re rho <= 27/32. This is more information than plugging in the
pointwise bound only on u>=200. It does not prove anything about the line
Re s=27/32 itself. B0 independently gives Re rho <=7/8 (OpenAIQRH,
Theorem 1.1, original PDF p.4). Symmetry gives 1-b <= Re rho <= b.
FiniteRH Theorem 1 (original PDF p.2, height 3000175332800), or
Platt–Trudgian Lemma 4 (p.4), puts the zeros up to H on the critical line.
Nontrivial zeros are counted with multiplicity. No real zero lies in
(0,1): the convergent alternating eta series is positive there and
equals (1-2^(1-s)) zeta(s) by continuation.

The following uses Dusart, §2.2.2 Theorem 2.3, original PDF p.5, as
stated there (positive ordinates, beta >= s). For s>=.77 and t>=H define
[
 \ell=\log H,\quad p={8\over3}(1-s),\quad q=5-2s,\quad
 d=1-p-q/\ell,\quad d_2=1-2/\ell,
]
[
 G_s=9.8 \,3^p \ell^q H^{p-1},\qquad C=103\ell^2/H .
]
Using log(1+z)<=z and (1+y/ell)^q<=exp(qy/ell), the number N_s(t)
of positive-ordinate zeros with real part >=s satisfies
[
 2N_s(He^y)/(He^y)\le G_s e^{-dy}+C e^{-d_2y}\qquad(y\ge0).
]
Both d,d_2 are positive. As N_s has no contribution at or below H, integrate
against -w'(t). For w=1/t the bound on 2 sum w is
D(s)=G_s/d+C/d_2. For w=1/t^2 it is
D_2(s)=(2/H)(G_s/(1+d)+C/(1+d_2)). For
w=min(1/t,2/(ht^2)), replace each factor 1/d by f(A,d), A=2/(Hh), where
[
 f(A,d)=\begin{cases}2A/(1+d),&A\le1,\\
 (1-A^{-d})/d+2A^{-d}/(1+d),&A\ge1.
 \end{cases}
]
This follows by splitting at y=log A; one can also take the minimum with
the undamped D(s). These bounds decrease as s increases: before any
linearization the majorants with p and q are monotone in s, and the
linearized count bound remains monotone at each y. For a fixed s the
undamped integral majorant for w=1/t also bounds the damped one.

For all positive ordinates >=H, the full count N(t) is at most
t log(t)/6 for t>=H. Indeed FKS Lemma 2.1 and Remark 2.2 (original
PDF pp.4–5, Rosser constants) bound the discrepancy from
(t/(2pi))log(t/(2pi e))+7/8 by .137 log t+.443 log log t+1.588.
Using the larger full count instead of the count above H in -w' integrals,
the bound on sum w (not twice the sum) is
[
 A_h=\begin{cases}
 A(\ell+1)/3,& A\le1,\\
 [\ell v+v^2/2+2(\ell+v+1)]/6,& A\ge1,\ v=\log A .
 \end{cases}
]
For the square weight use A_2=10/H, by the same integration with
2/t^3: the integral is (ell+1)/(3H)<10/H. For the default h=e^(-u/4)
we can use the simpler
[
 U(u)=((u/4)^2/2+32(u/4)+64)/6
]
in place of A_h (ell<29, log A<=u/4). For low ordinates twice the
sum of 1/gamma is <116: use FKS Table 1 and Lemma 2.1 with
T0=30610046000 and H. For twice the sum of 1/gamma^2 use .1: the first
ordinate exceeds 14 (CH2 §B.1, original PDF p.43), FKS Table 1 at
100 gives a reciprocal sum <.5922435112, and CH2 Lemma B.5 (p.44)
bounds the tail above 100. The strict numerical inequalities are in
certify.py. Endpoint ordinates, if present in these statements, can
be handled by including the equality in the high bin and by taking a
one-sided limit in the count bound.

Let s_0=.77, with grid s_j=j/800 starting at j=616 and ending at
j=800b, an integer in both cases. If A is the chosen bound for all
high ordinates and D_j a bound for twice the sum of their weights at
Re rho >=s_j, use
[
 F_b(u)=C_{lo}e^{-u/2}+A(e^{-s_0u}+e^{-(1-s_0)u})+
 \sum_{j=616}^{800b-1}\min(A,D_j)
 (e^{-(1-s_{j+1})u}-e^{-(1-s_j)u}).                      \tag{S}
]
To prove it, pair beta and 1-beta at each positive ordinate.
Their normalized exponential sum is at most e^(-s0 u)+e^(-(1-s0)u)
if beta<=s0 on the right of the pair, by convexity. Above s0 the
excess is at most the increase in the right-hand exponential
(the left-hand exponential decreases). Layer integration, or its
left-bin upper sum in (S), counts each right-hand zero twice after
including negative ordinates. This extra weighted count is at most
A as well as D_j. Zeros on the critical line obey the same base bound.
Thus (S) bounds the sum over both signs with weights w; no
independence of terms in an explicit formula is used. One may also
use the weighted layer integral instead of the upper grid sum.
The code collects coefficients: the base at exponent 1-s0 has
coefficient A-min(A,D_616), the intermediate coefficients are
successive nonnegative differences, and the last coefficient is
min(A,D_(800b-1)).

Dusart (2.1), original PDF pp.3–4, gives the classical explicit
formula with midpoint values at jumps. Its use here is only under
integration. For clarity, the series also converges in L^2 on every
compact interval of u>0. Choose a smooth nonnegative bump at least
1 on the interval. In a unit frequency bin the sum of absolute
coefficients is O(log(2+|j|)/(1+|j|)) by the count bound (the local
count is O(log t)). Integration of each product against the bump
twice by parts bounds its cross-bin integral by a constant times
(1+|j-k|)^(-2); the real parts of the exponentials range in a compact
set. The inequality 2 a_j a_k <=a_j^2+a_k^2 proves the Cauchy
statement. The L^2 limit agrees almost everywhere with (2.1) by
an almost-everywhere convergent subsequence and the given pointwise
formula off prime powers. This justifies averaging term by term.
The arguments below with finite integrals followed by limits are
also legitimate: the integrated coefficients are absolutely
summable by the square-frequency count bound.

An explicit continuous-layer alternative for u>=140 is
[
 E_{\rm cont}(u)=(1+2h)\{h/2+116 e^{-u/2}
       +U(u)(e^{-s_0u}+e^{-(1-s_0)u})
       +D(b){u\over u-97}e^{-a u}\}+2e^{-u}.
]
Indeed |(log(G_s/d))'|<= (8/3)(ell+log 3)+2 log ell
+ (8/3+2/ell)/d(s0)<97; the other term in D is constant. Thus
D(s)<=D(b)e^(97(b-s)), and direct integration proves the formula.
The limit of this coefficient after division by e^(-a u) is D(b).
Numerically D(7/8)<.006740 and D(27/32)<.118073 (direct interval
evaluation of dat in profiles.py); these are coefficients of a
proved majorant, not lower bounds on the arithmetic error.

For the default E_h and E_cont, their quotients by e^(-a u) decrease
on u>=140. For the grid version, U(140)>2D(s0), and U'/U<=2/u, so
(U-D(s0))'/ (U-D(s0))<=4/u. The base exponents after factoring are
>=.23-a, and 4/140<.23-a for both caps. The remaining coefficients
are nonnegative constants (including the last); the factors
1+2h and u/(u-97) in the respective bounds are decreasing.
More generally multiplying the unnormalized bounds by u^m preserves
monotonic decrease on u>=max(140,(m+4)/a); this follows by applying
the logarithmic derivative estimate to each positive term. These
are whole-ray checks, not extrapolations from tabulated points.

def continuous_spectral(u,cap):
    """Closed majorant for continuous density integration; u>=140."""
    u=I(u)
    h=ef(I('.25'),u); A=U(u)
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    return (1+2*h)*(h/2+CL*ef(I('.5'),u)+A*(ef(s0,u)+ef(1-s0,u))
           +dat(cap)[0]*u/(u-97)*ef(a,u))+2*ef(1,u)

Initially take B^+(v)=J_b(v)-.988 e^(-v/2) and
B^-(v)=J_b(v)+T(v), meaning
[
 -B^-(v)\ le v e^{-v}\pi(e^v)-A_*(v)\ \le B^+(v).
]
To prove this, first use J(x)=sum_(p^k<=x) 1/k. Partial summation
against psi gives the normalized error for J as
[

      \int_{\log2}^{v} e^w g(w)\,dw/w^2\right).
]
For w<=20 use |g(w)|<1.5e^(-w/2) from CH2 Lemma 9.2, which
includes w down to log 2; splitting at w=2 bounds the absolute
early integral plus 2/log 2 and .1 by 17000. The .1 covers the
constant/trivial-zero part from w=20 to infinity before normalization.
On [20,v] integrate each term e^(rho w)/w^2 by parts using
1/rho. For beta>=1/8 the derivative of e^(beta w)/w^2 is at least
(beta-.1)e^(beta w)/w^2; hence the bound on the integral after
division by 1/|rho| is at most
e^(beta v)/v^2 times 1+1+.1/(beta-.1)<=6. Use (P) of spectral.md
for the square frequency sum. These finite integrals have the
justification given there. For primes powers,
[
 .988e^{-v/2} \le v e^{-v}(J(e^v)-\pi(e^v))\le T(v).
]
For k=2 the lower bound is theta(e^(v/2))/(v/2), times 1/2,

increasing order, detect whether p survived the smaller primes,
and remove p times a surviving integer >=p. The quotient floor

def primepi(n):
    # Each distinct floor(n/k) or small integer is a key.
    rt=isqrt(n)
    vals=[n//k for k in range(1,n//(rt+1)+1)]+list(range(rt,0,-1))
    C={v:v-1 for v in vals}
    for p in range(2,rt+1):
        if C[p]==C[p-1]: continue
        a=C[p-1]
        for v in vals:
            if v<p*p: break
            C[v]-=C[v//p]-a
    return C[n]

        U=I(u)

        assert (ideal-los-target).r<0
        print('fixed log onset, k, B0 certified coefficient, D02 full coefficient:',u,k,m0,dN[k])

For real x>1 put u=log x. The counted primes and prime powers
include equality. The four errors treated here, in order, are
[
 |e^\gamma u P_{raw}(x)-1|,quad
 |e^{-\gamma}Q_{raw}(x)/u-1|,quad
 |\sum_{p\le x}1/p-\log u-M|,quad
 |\sum_{p\le x}(\log p)/p-u+B_3|.
]
Here M=gamma+sum_p(log(1-1/p)+1/p), and
B_3=gamma+sum_p log(p)/(p(p-1)) (Dusart, original PDF pp.17–18,
Theorems 5.6–5.7). Gamma is Euler's constant. The other two are
reciprocals after normalizing; the four are not independent results
from unrelated trials.

def outputs(u,cap):
    u=I(u)
    w=werr(u,cap)
    S=primitive(u,cap)
    wneg=w
    if u.l>=I(10000).ln().r and u.r<=I(10**13).ln().l:
        wneg=mini(w,I('.751')*ef(I('.5'),u)+S)
    z=w/u+S/u**2
    zn=wneg/u+S/u**2
    if u.l>I(10**9).ln().r:
        for adaptive in (False,True):
            T=evalT(u,adaptive)
            if u.l<=T.ln().r:continue
            Q=ch(u,True,adaptive)/u+3*ef(99,u)/u
            z=mini(z,Q)
            zn=mini(zn,Q+PI**2/(3*T*T*u*u))
    l1,h1,l0,h0,ld,hd=prime_powers(u)
    A=I((ld-zn).l,(hd+z).r)
    a,b=I(A.l),I(A.r)
    P=maxi(-expm1(-b),expm1(-a))
    Q=maxi(-expm1(a),expm1(b))
    return P,Q,maxi(h0+z,zn-l0),maxi(h1+w,wneg-l1)

Let Z_1(u)=sum_(n<=e^u) Lambda(n)/n -u+gamma and
Z_0(u)=sum_(2<=n<=e^u) Lambda(n)/(n log n)-log u-gamma. Then
[
 Z_1=g(u)-\int_u^\infty g(v)dv,\qquad
 Z_0=Z_1(u)/u-\int_u^\infty Z_1(v)\,dv/v^2.           \tag{M1}
]
For the first identity, partial summation gives
sum Lambda(n)/n=1+g+u+int_0^u g. The constant 1+int_0^infty g=-gamma
follows by letting s tend to 1 in the Euler identity in spectral.md:
the Laurent constant of -zeta'/zeta is -gamma (also used in
CH2 Proposition 9.1 proof, eq. (6.7)). The existence of the
integral follows from the spectral tail. For the second identity,
the Stieltjes derivative of Z_0 is (1/u) times that of Z_1.
Both normalized limits at infinity are zero: for Z_0 this follows,
for example, from Dusart Theorem 5.6 and its constant formula,
subtracting the prime-power tail from log Q_raw. Integrate by
parts over (u,infinity), so the value at u is right-continuous.

For a zero with beta<1 the two contributions to Z_1 in (M1)
combine to e^((rho-1)u)/(1-rho). In the tail of the second
identity, the additional denominator can be recovered despite
the factor 1/v^2: for Re lambda>0,
[
 \left|\int_u^\infty e^{-\lambda v}\,{dv\over v^2}\right|
 \le {e^{-u\Re\lambda}\over |\lambda|u^2}.
]
Use 1/v^2=int_0^infty t e^(-t v)dt and |lambda+t|>=|lambda|.
Combined with absolute summability after integration, this bounds
the absolute tail in (M1) by S_b(u)/u^2. The trivial part of
Z_1 is bounded by 2e^(-u) (the -log(2pi) contributions cancel).
As in spectral.md, the formula under integration ignores the
countable jumps but the endpoints themselves use the actual
right-hand values. This is an advantage over absolute integration
of the original psi majorant; no loss by a factor about 1/a
is needed on the leading endpoint term.

Define
\[
 U_j(x)=\sum_{k\ge2}\sum_{p>x^{1/k}} w_j(p,k),\qquad
 w_0=1/(k p^k),\quad w_1=(\log p)/p^k;
\]
let T_0(x)=sum_(k>=2,p>x) w_0 and D_0=U_0-T_0. All these are
nonnegative and U_0<=U_1/u. The signed errors are exactly
[
 \log(e^{-\gamma}Q_{raw}/u)=Z_0+D_0,qquad
 \sum_{p\le x}1/p-\log u-M=Z_0+U_0,qquad
 \sum_{p\le x}\log(p)/p-u+B_3=Z_1+U_1.               \tag{M2}
]
Thus tails are not an extra independent symmetric uncertainty
for both ends. For an interval [l,h] on the first signed log error,
the two product bounds, in the order above, are
max(1-e^(-h),e^(-l)-1) and max(1-e^l,e^h-1).

Here are explicit signed prime-power bounds valid for x>=2.
Let c=1.0001 (Dusart p.13, proof of Proposition 4.4 has a
slightly better value), and t(v)=max(0,1-delta(v)), where
delta(v) is the minimum of the eligible Dusart Theorem 4.2
bounds eta_k/v^k for arguments >=e^v. Use its k=0 bound for
all v>=0. Then t is nondecreasing, theta(y)<=cy, and
theta(y)>=t(v)y for all y>=e^v. For k=2 or 3, put v=u/k and
Y_k=e^(-(k-1)v). Applying Stieltjes summation over p>e^v,
the two bounds for the w_1 tail are
\[
 Y_k[,t(v)k/(k-1)-c,]_+,qquad
 Y_k[c,k/(k-1)-t(v)].
\]
The same formulas work at k=4. For w_0 use the decreasing
weight f(y)=1/(k y^k log y) in the Stieltjes integral. The main
integral divided by Y_k lies between
\[
 m_-=[d(1-d)]_+/k,qquad m_+=\min(d,d(1-d+2d^2))/k,
 \quad d=1/((k-1)v).
\]
Expand 1/(v+w) geometrically with signed remainder under an
exponential integral. The signed bounds on the tail are
Y_k[t(v)m_-+(t(v)-c)/(k v)]_+ and
Y_k[c m_++(c-t(v))/(k v)], using the endpoint contributions
from Stieltjes summation. For T_0 use its k=2 term with v=u as
the lower bound, and the upper on that term divided by
1-e^(-u) as the upper.

For k>=4 put z=x^(1/4). If p>z, use the k=4 bound for w_1
divided by 1-1/z. For p<=z the first retained prime power is
>x, so summing the geometric progression costs at most
[theta(z)+sum_(p<=z) log p/(p-1)]/x. The sum inside is at
most 2c(1+max(0,log(z/2))) by partial summation and
p/(p-1)<=2. Divide the resulting w_1 upper by u for w_0.
Use zero as lower for k>=4. These formulas are implemented
in prime_powers(). In particular U_1/e^(-u/2) has the supplied
nonincreasing upper function on u>=16: the remaining factors
are e^(-u/6), e^(-u/4), the decreasing geometric factor,
and (1+max(0,u/4-log 2))e^(-u/2), with coefficients using the
nonincreasing delta. Hence U_1<=1.111 e^(-u/2) on x>=10^7.
This includes the finite joins of all the large power rows.

eta_rows=[
(1,0,'1'),(2,1,'1.2323'),(908994923,1,'.001'),

(2,4,'151.3')]
eta_rows=[(I(x).ln(),k,I(eta)) for x,k,eta in eta_rows]
def theta_lower(v):
    return maxi(0,1-mini(*[eta/v**k for a,k,eta in eta_rows if v.l>=a.r or k==0]))

def squaretail(v,k,weighted=True):
    Y=ef(k-1,v)
    t=theta_lower(v)
    if weighted:
        return maxi(0,t*k/(k-1)-c0)*Y,(c0*k/(k-1)-t)*Y
    # integral 1/k*int exp(-(k-1)w)/w dw
    d=1/((k-1)*v)
    mainlo=maxi(0,d*(1-d))/k
    mainhi=mini(d,d*(1-d+2*d*d))/k
    lo=maxi(0,t*mainlo+(t-c0)/(k*v))*Y
    hi=(c0*mainhi+(c0-t)/(k*v))*Y
    return lo,hi

def prime_powers(u):
    u=I(u)
    # k>=4, split p<=x^(1/4) and p>x^(1/4)
    v=u/4
    _,f4=squaretail(v,4)
    r4=c0*(ef(I('.75'),u)+2*(1+maxi(0,v-LN2))*ef(1,u))+f4/(1-ef(1,v))
    a,b=squaretail(u/2,2)
    c,d=squaretail(u/3,3)
    lo1,hi1=a+c,b+d+r4
    a,b=squaretail(u/2,2,False)
    c,d=squaretail(u/3,3,False)
    lo0,hi0=a+c,b+d+r4/u
    a,b=squaretail(u,2,False)
    return lo1,hi1,lo0,hi0,maxi(0,lo0-b/(1-ef(1,u))),hi0-a

def mertens_tails():
    a=I(10**7).ln()
    b=I(10**13).ln()

    pu=(prime_powers(a)[1]/ef(I('.5'),a)).r
    assert pu<D('1.111')

    ww=I('.791')+s+I('1.111')
    zz=ww+s/a
    w=ww*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    z=zz*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    assert w.r<D('.165')
    assert (z*(zz*ef(I('.5'),a)/a).exp()).r<D('.166')

  rows with k>=2, apply (5.7) and the proof of Theorem 5.7:
  r=eta_k/(k u^k)+eta_k(1+1/(k+1))/u^(k+1) for the
  reciprocal sum, and eta_k/((k-1)u^(k-1))+eta_k/u^k for the
  weighted sum. The signed log-product interval is
  [-r-T_0^+,r-T_0^-]. Select the smaller eligible row, not
  just k=3. More generally if e_theta^±(v) are pointwise
  one-sided relative theta errors, integrate the available
  past-cutoff envelopes against 1/v+1/v^2 for sum 1/p and
  against 1 for log p/p; the endpoint terms are e_theta^±(u)/u
  and e_theta^±(u). Use the opposite sign for the integral,
  as in Dusart (5.7). Besides the table, one can take finite
  RH theta or E_b and Dusart 4.3/4.5 for the admitted
  one-sided prime-power corrections. Minima are taken only
  on their valid domains; this integral version preserves
  pointwise improvements without extending a finite estimate
  to infinity. It is an alternative to (M1) which retains
  a useful oscillation cancellation.

def theta_transfers(u):
    u=I(u)
    bs=[]; bws=[]
    for a,k,eta in eta_rows:
        if k<2 or a.r>u.l:continue
        bs.append(eta/(k*u**k)+eta*(1+I(1)/(k+1))/u**(k+1))
        bws.append(eta/((k-1)*u**(k-1))+eta/u**k)
    if not bs: return None
    r=mini(*bs); wr=mini(*bws)
    aa,bb=squaretail(u,2,False)
    bb/=1-ef(1,u)
    return maxi(-expm1(-r+aa),expm1(r+bb)),maxi(-expm1(-r-bb),expm1(r-aa)),r,wr

def squaretail(v,k,weighted=True):
    Y=ef(k-1,v)
    t=theta_lower(v)
    if weighted:
        return maxi(0,t*k/(k-1)-c0)*Y,(c0*k/(k-1)-t)*Y
    # integral 1/k*int exp(-(k-1)w)/w dw
    d=1/((k-1)*v)
    mainlo=maxi(0,d*(1-d))/k
    mainhi=mini(d,d*(1-d+2*d*d))/k
    lo=maxi(0,t*mainlo+(t-c0)/(k*v))*Y
    hi=(c0*mainhi+(c0-t)/(k*v))*Y
    return lo,hi

    a,b=squaretail(u,2,False)

## Proof of the finite checks

The deterministic Eratosthenes sieve goes to 25000000, marking
multiples beginning at p^2 through floor(sqrt LIMIT); it includes
1565927 primes (see sieve digest in finite_run.txt).
The four cumulative quantities are obtained by multiplying
p/(p-1), adding 1/p and adding log(p)/p; use intervals
enclosing those three followed by the indicated normalization.
There is no rounding of primes, no random prime tests, and no
use of a sampled grid of large x.

Here are details of the normalizer intervals:
* For gamma start with H_N-log N-1/(2N)+1/(12N^2), N=20000.
  Its excess over gamma is in [0,1/(20(N-1)^4)]. Indeed for
  f(t)=1/t on each cell [k,k+1], set z=1/(2k+1).
  The excess of the trapezoid over the integral is
  2 sum_(j>=1) [2j/(2j+1)] z^(2j+1).
  The derivative correction (f'(k+1)-f'(k))/12 is
  (4/3) z^3/(1-z^2)^2. The leading coefficients match;
  each later correction coefficient is larger, and their
  aggregate excess is <=5z^5 for k>=N. Sum with
  z<1/(2k), telescope the trapezoids and derivatives,
  and bound the tail by an integral.
* Compute the initial prime sums defining M and B3 through
  Y=25000000. The remaining weighted B3 tail has main term
  -log(1-1/Y). For its decreasing weight f(t)=1/(t(t-1))
  in the Stieltjes integral against theta, the absolute error
  from this main integral is at most
  delta(Y)[2Yf(Y)+integral_Y^infty f],
  where delta(Y)=.2/(log Y)^2 by Dusart Table in Theorem 4.2,
  valid for all t>=Y. For the M tail f(t)=
  (-log(1-1/t)-1/t)/log t. Bound its main integral between that
  of 1/(2t^2 log t) and that integral times 1/(1-1/Y);
  bound the two endpoint terms using 2Yf(Y)<=1/((Y-1)log Y).
  The alternating geometric integral through terms 14 and 15
  rigorously encloses the main integral as in mertens.md.
  These operations give the intervals in the receipt, without
  taking published decimal M,B3 approximations as exact.

Between successive prime events the error signs can change,
but the normalized *signed* functions multiplied by u^3
(or u^2) are monotone. For the P signed function use
d((c u-1)u^3)/du=u^2(4c u-3) with c u=1/Qhat>.75.
For Q use d((c/u-1)u^3)/du=u(2c-3u) with Qhat<1.5.
For the reciprocal sum use u^2(3(error_signed)-1);
for the last sum use u(2(error_signed)-u).
The code checks guards .8<Qhat<1.3, reciprocal signed error
<.1 and weighted signed error <1 at both ends for x>=10000.
Since each unscaled function is monotone on a prime slab,
the guards and hence these derivative signs hold throughout.
Thus the maximum modulus is at one of the two endpoints,
including the *left limit* at a prime and the actual value
at the prime separately. This proves full slab coverage;
the additional queried nonprime threshold values and root
brackets are handled the same way.

finite_run.txt reports the last endpoints not certified at
each threshold. Any next prime from finite_joins.py and both
sides of every later prime pass, so all slabs from that next
prime pass. There may be a better onset inside the preceding
slab, as demonstrated by the zoom. Endpoints printed to nine
decimals are rounded up by interval arithmetic. The certificate
requires the standard Decimal correctness for exp and ln,
and normal interval arithmetic; it is not a source-first
formal proof of program execution.

* At x>=2278383, the reciprocal sum coefficient can be .199917,
  rather than .2.
* At x>=912560, the weighted sum coefficient can be .29999948,
  rather than .3. At x>=1000000 it can be .295973.

Fixing the original coefficients instead, the following earlier
real onsets suffice (rounding the upper root enclosures upwards):

| Error | coefficient | safe closed real onset |
|---|---:|---:|

|Q |.2|2278381.71114184102|

These are not integer endpoint substitutes. The near-onset
root brackets in zoom_run.txt also prove failure at the lower
side of each bracket; the normalized error crosses a continuous
piece. All later prime/slab endpoints are accounted for.
If both products are wanted with the same .2 margin and
the same onset, use the Q row.

        ('Q inverse log .2',D('2278381'),D('2278382'),I('.2'),lambda L:(P/(cg*L)-1)*L**3),
        ('reciprocal sum inverse log .2',D('2278382'),D('2278383'),I('.2'),lambda L:(a-L.ln()-M)*L**3),
        ('weighted sum inverse log .3',D('912559'),D('912560'),I('.3'),lambda L:(b-L+B)*L**2),
    )

        assert z(l).l>0>z(r).r

            elif z(w).l>0:l=w
            else:

                a1=(l+w)/2
                b1=(r+w)/2
                moved=False
                if z(a1).l>0:l=a1;moved=True
                if z(b1).r<0:r=b1;moved=True
                if not moved:break

def mertens_tails():
    a=I(10**7).ln()
    b=I(10**13).ln()
    # The U1 bound divided by exp(-u/2) is decreasing on u>=16.
    pu=(prime_powers(a)[1]/ef(I('.5'),a)).r
    assert pu<D('1.111')
    s=I('.1')+I(20)/H*ef(-I(3)/8,b)+2*ef(I('.5'),a)
    ww=I('.791')+s+I('1.111')
    zz=ww+s/a
    w=ww*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    z=zz*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    assert w.r<D('.165')
    assert (z*(zz*ef(I('.5'),a)/a).exp()).r<D('.166')
    # Sharper signed reciprocal-power tail at the 25-million join:
    t25=I(25000000).ln()
    z25=(I('.791')+s+s/t25)*t25*t25*ef(I('.5'),t25)+prime_powers(t25)[3]*t25**3
    assert (z25*(z25/t25**3).exp()).r<D('.10994')
    print('M sharper coefficient at x=25000000, products and reciprocal sum: .10994')
    # Normalize the finite-li transfer and the tail after its cutoff.
    # Check the psi-to-pi bounds used to obtain the remaining integral after CUT.
    e=I('113.67')+I('.6')/CUT+17000*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+powterm(CUT)/ef(I('.5'),CUT)
    f=PI/H+120/(H*CUT)*ef(I('.125'),CUT)+12/CUT*ef(1,CUT)
    assert e.r<D(116) and f.r<D('1.06e-12')
    m=I(190)
    a0=I('.125')
    rr=spectral(m,basecap)/ef(a0,m)
    assert (rr+(17000*m*ef(1,m)+powterm(m)+6*spec_simple_prim(m,basecap)/m)/ef(a0,m)).r<D('.014')
    t=pi_after_cut()
    assert (I('1.95')+I('3.9')/b+I('19.5')/b**2).r<D('2.11')
    def pi_C(x):
        z=I('6.33')*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)+(4*x+2)*x*x*ef(1,x)+CUT*CUT*t
        q=(z+x*x*ef(1,x))/(1-ef(1,x))
        return q*(q/x**3).exp()
    assert pi_C(b).r<D('.002')
    for u,c in ((32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017')):
        assert pi_C(I(u)).r<D(c)
    ww=(I('114.1')+I('1.111'))*CUT*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+(PI/H+I(20)/H*ef(a0,CUT)+2*ef(1,CUT))*190**2
    zz=ww+spec_simple_prim(CUT,basecap)*190
    assert (zz*(zz/CUT**3).exp()).r<D('.00008')
    for u,c in ((17,'.117'),(18,'.079'),(19,'.053'),(20,'.036'),(21,'.024'),(22,'.016'),(23,'.011'),
                (24,'.007'),(25,'.0045'),(26,'.003'),(27,'.002'),(28,'.002')):
        x=I(u)
        v=(I('.791')+s+prime_powers(x)[1]/ef(I('.5'),x)+s/x)*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)
        assert (v*(v/x**3).exp()).r<D(c)
        print('M inverse-log whole-ray coefficient, log onset',u,c)
    print('M extra medium-level full ray C:',(32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017'),('log(10^19)','.00008'))
    # Power-tail rows: all absolute product/sum errors <= coefficient times X^(-alpha)/L
    # except logp/p, which has no division by L.

  and .199973 (Q), respectively, rather than .2.
* At x>=2278383, the reciprocal sum coefficient can be .199917,
  rather than .2.
* At x>=912560, the weighted sum coefficient can be .29999948,
  rather than .3. At x>=1000000 it can be .295973.

Fixing the original coefficients instead, the following earlier
real onsets suffice (rounding the upper root enclosures upwards):

| Error | coefficient | safe closed real onset |
|---|---:|---:|
|P |.2|2278381.575555466|
|Q |.2|2278381.71114184102|
|sum 1/p|.2|2278382.113038|
|sum log p/p|.3|912559.997437|

These are not integer endpoint substitutes. The near-onset
root brackets in zoom_run.txt also prove failure at the lower
side of each bracket; the normalized error crosses a continuous
piece. All later prime/slab endpoints are accounted for.
If both products are wanted with the same .2 margin and
the same onset, use the Q row.

    funcs=(
        ('P inverse log .2',D('2278381'),D('2278382'),I('.2'),lambda L:(1-cg*L/P)*L**3),
        ('Q inverse log .2',D('2278381'),D('2278382'),I('.2'),lambda L:(P/(cg*L)-1)*L**3),
        ('reciprocal sum inverse log .2',D('2278382'),D('2278383'),I('.2'),lambda L:(a-L.ln()-M)*L**3),
        ('weighted sum inverse log .3',D('912559'),D('912560'),I('.3'),lambda L:(b-L+B)*L**2),
    )
    for name,l,r,m,f in funcs:
        def z(x):return f(I(x).ln())-m
        assert z(l).l>0>z(r).r

            if z(w).r<0:r=w
            elif z(w).l>0:l=w
            else:

                a1=(l+w)/2
                b1=(r+w)/2
                moved=False
                if z(a1).l>0:l=a1;moved=True
                if z(b1).r<0:r=b1;moved=True
                if not moved:break

def mertens_tails():
    a=I(10**7).ln()
    b=I(10**13).ln()
    # The U1 bound divided by exp(-u/2) is decreasing on u>=16.
    pu=(prime_powers(a)[1]/ef(I('.5'),a)).r
    assert pu<D('1.111')
    s=I('.1')+I(20)/H*ef(-I(3)/8,b)+2*ef(I('.5'),a)
    ww=I('.791')+s+I('1.111')
    zz=ww+s/a
    w=ww*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    z=zz*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    assert w.r<D('.165')
    assert (z*(zz*ef(I('.5'),a)/a).exp()).r<D('.166')
    # Sharper signed reciprocal-power tail at the 25-million join:
    t25=I(25000000).ln()
    z25=(I('.791')+s+s/t25)*t25*t25*ef(I('.5'),t25)+prime_powers(t25)[3]*t25**3
    assert (z25*(z25/t25**3).exp()).r<D('.10994')
    print('M sharper coefficient at x=25000000, products and reciprocal sum: .10994')
    # Normalize the finite-li transfer and the tail after its cutoff.
    # Check the psi-to-pi bounds used to obtain the remaining integral after CUT.
    e=I('113.67')+I('.6')/CUT+17000*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+powterm(CUT)/ef(I('.5'),CUT)
    f=PI/H+120/(H*CUT)*ef(I('.125'),CUT)+12/CUT*ef(1,CUT)
    assert e.r<D(116) and f.r<D('1.06e-12')
    m=I(190)
    a0=I('.125')
    rr=spectral(m,basecap)/ef(a0,m)
    assert (rr+(17000*m*ef(1,m)+powterm(m)+6*spec_simple_prim(m,basecap)/m)/ef(a0,m)).r<D('.014')
    t=pi_after_cut()
    assert (I('1.95')+I('3.9')/b+I('19.5')/b**2).r<D('2.11')
    def pi_C(x):
        z=I('6.33')*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)+(4*x+2)*x*x*ef(1,x)+CUT*CUT*t
        q=(z+x*x*ef(1,x))/(1-ef(1,x))
        return q*(q/x**3).exp()
    assert pi_C(b).r<D('.002')
    for u,c in ((32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017')):
        assert pi_C(I(u)).r<D(c)
    ww=(I('114.1')+I('1.111'))*CUT*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+(PI/H+I(20)/H*ef(a0,CUT)+2*ef(1,CUT))*190**2
    zz=ww+spec_simple_prim(CUT,basecap)*190
    assert (zz*(zz/CUT**3).exp()).r<D('.00008')
    for u,c in ((17,'.117'),(18,'.079'),(19,'.053'),(20,'.036'),(21,'.024'),(22,'.016'),(23,'.011'),
                (24,'.007'),(25,'.0045'),(26,'.003'),(27,'.002'),(28,'.002')):
        x=I(u)
        v=(I('.791')+s+prime_powers(x)[1]/ef(I('.5'),x)+s/x)*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)
        assert (v*(v/x**3).exp()).r<D(c)
        print('M inverse-log whole-ray coefficient, log onset',u,c)
    print('M extra medium-level full ray C:',(32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017'),('log(10^19)','.00008'))
    # Power-tail rows: all absolute product/sum errors <= coefficient times X^(-alpha)/L
    # except logp/p, which has no division by L.

def mertens_tails():
    a=I(10**7).ln()
    b=I(10**13).ln()
    # The U1 bound divided by exp(-u/2) is decreasing on u>=16.
    pu=(prime_powers(a)[1]/ef(I('.5'),a)).r
    assert pu<D('1.111')
    s=I('.1')+I(20)/H*ef(-I(3)/8,b)+2*ef(I('.5'),a)
    ww=I('.791')+s+I('1.111')
    zz=ww+s/a
    w=ww*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    z=zz*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    assert w.r<D('.165')
    assert (z*(zz*ef(I('.5'),a)/a).exp()).r<D('.166')
    # Sharper signed reciprocal-power tail at the 25-million join:
    t25=I(25000000).ln()
    z25=(I('.791')+s+s/t25)*t25*t25*ef(I('.5'),t25)+prime_powers(t25)[3]*t25**3
    assert (z25*(z25/t25**3).exp()).r<D('.10994')
    print('M sharper coefficient at x=25000000, products and reciprocal sum: .10994')
    # Normalize the finite-li transfer and the tail after its cutoff.
    # Check the psi-to-pi bounds used to obtain the remaining integral after CUT.
    e=I('113.67')+I('.6')/CUT+17000*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+powterm(CUT)/ef(I('.5'),CUT)
    f=PI/H+120/(H*CUT)*ef(I('.125'),CUT)+12/CUT*ef(1,CUT)
    assert e.r<D(116) and f.r<D('1.06e-12')
    m=I(190)
    a0=I('.125')
    rr=spectral(m,basecap)/ef(a0,m)
    assert (rr+(17000*m*ef(1,m)+powterm(m)+6*spec_simple_prim(m,basecap)/m)/ef(a0,m)).r<D('.014')
    t=pi_after_cut()
    assert (I('1.95')+I('3.9')/b+I('19.5')/b**2).r<D('2.11')
    def pi_C(x):
        z=I('6.33')*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)+(4*x+2)*x*x*ef(1,x)+CUT*CUT*t
        q=(z+x*x*ef(1,x))/(1-ef(1,x))
        return q*(q/x**3).exp()
    assert pi_C(b).r<D('.002')
    for u,c in ((32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017')):
        assert pi_C(I(u)).r<D(c)
    ww=(I('114.1')+I('1.111'))*CUT*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+(PI/H+I(20)/H*ef(a0,CUT)+2*ef(1,CUT))*190**2
    zz=ww+spec_simple_prim(CUT,basecap)*190
    assert (zz*(zz/CUT**3).exp()).r<D('.00008')
    for u,c in ((17,'.117'),(18,'.079'),(19,'.053'),(20,'.036'),(21,'.024'),(22,'.016'),(23,'.011'),
                (24,'.007'),(25,'.0045'),(26,'.003'),(27,'.002'),(28,'.002')):
        x=I(u)
        v=(I('.791')+s+prime_powers(x)[1]/ef(I('.5'),x)+s/x)*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)
        assert (v*(v/x**3).exp()).r<D(c)
        print('M inverse-log whole-ray coefficient, log onset',u,c)
    print('M extra medium-level full ray C:',(32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017'),('log(10^19)','.00008'))
    # Power-tail rows: all absolute product/sum errors <= coefficient times X^(-alpha)/L
    # except logp/p, which has no division by L.

def mertens_tails():
    a=I(10**7).ln()
    b=I(10**13).ln()
    # The U1 bound divided by exp(-u/2) is decreasing on u>=16.
    pu=(prime_powers(a)[1]/ef(I('.5'),a)).r
    assert pu<D('1.111')
    s=I('.1')+I(20)/H*ef(-I(3)/8,b)+2*ef(I('.5'),a)
    ww=I('.791')+s+I('1.111')
    zz=ww+s/a
    w=ww*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    z=zz*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    assert w.r<D('.165')
    assert (z*(zz*ef(I('.5'),a)/a).exp()).r<D('.166')
    # Sharper signed reciprocal-power tail at the 25-million join:
    t25=I(25000000).ln()
    z25=(I('.791')+s+s/t25)*t25*t25*ef(I('.5'),t25)+prime_powers(t25)[3]*t25**3
    assert (z25*(z25/t25**3).exp()).r<D('.10994')
    print('M sharper coefficient at x=25000000, products and reciprocal sum: .10994')
    # Normalize the finite-li transfer and the tail after its cutoff.
    # Check the psi-to-pi bounds used to obtain the remaining integral after CUT.
    e=I('113.67')+I('.6')/CUT+17000*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+powterm(CUT)/ef(I('.5'),CUT)
    f=PI/H+120/(H*CUT)*ef(I('.125'),CUT)+12/CUT*ef(1,CUT)
    assert e.r<D(116) and f.r<D('1.06e-12')
    m=I(190)
    a0=I('.125')
    rr=spectral(m,basecap)/ef(a0,m)
    assert (rr+(17000*m*ef(1,m)+powterm(m)+6*spec_simple_prim(m,basecap)/m)/ef(a0,m)).r<D('.014')
    t=pi_after_cut()
    assert (I('1.95')+I('3.9')/b+I('19.5')/b**2).r<D('2.11')
    def pi_C(x):
        z=I('6.33')*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)+(4*x+2)*x*x*ef(1,x)+CUT*CUT*t
        q=(z+x*x*ef(1,x))/(1-ef(1,x))
        return q*(q/x**3).exp()
    assert pi_C(b).r<D('.002')
    for u,c in ((32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017')):
        assert pi_C(I(u)).r<D(c)
    ww=(I('114.1')+I('1.111'))*CUT*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+(PI/H+I(20)/H*ef(a0,CUT)+2*ef(1,CUT))*190**2
    zz=ww+spec_simple_prim(CUT,basecap)*190
    assert (zz*(zz/CUT**3).exp()).r<D('.00008')
    for u,c in ((17,'.117'),(18,'.079'),(19,'.053'),(20,'.036'),(21,'.024'),(22,'.016'),(23,'.011'),
                (24,'.007'),(25,'.0045'),(26,'.003'),(27,'.002'),(28,'.002')):
        x=I(u)
        v=(I('.791')+s+prime_powers(x)[1]/ef(I('.5'),x)+s/x)*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)
        assert (v*(v/x**3).exp()).r<D(c)
        print('M inverse-log whole-ray coefficient, log onset',u,c)
    print('M extra medium-level full ray C:',(32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017'),('log(10^19)','.00008'))
    # Power-tail rows: all absolute product/sum errors <= coefficient times X^(-alpha)/L
    # except logp/p, which has no division by L.

def mertens_tails():
    a=I(10**7).ln()
    b=I(10**13).ln()
    # The U1 bound divided by exp(-u/2) is decreasing on u>=16.
    pu=(prime_powers(a)[1]/ef(I('.5'),a)).r
    assert pu<D('1.111')
    s=I('.1')+I(20)/H*ef(-I(3)/8,b)+2*ef(I('.5'),a)
    ww=I('.791')+s+I('1.111')
    zz=ww+s/a
    w=ww*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    z=zz*a*a*ef(I('.5'),a)
    assert w.r<D('.165')
    assert (z*(zz*ef(I('.5'),a)/a).exp()).r<D('.166')
    # Sharper signed reciprocal-power tail at the 25-million join:
    t25=I(25000000).ln()
    z25=(I('.791')+s+s/t25)*t25*t25*ef(I('.5'),t25)+prime_powers(t25)[3]*t25**3
    assert (z25*(z25/t25**3).exp()).r<D('.10994')
    print('M sharper coefficient at x=25000000, products and reciprocal sum: .10994')
    # Normalize the finite-li transfer and the tail after its cutoff.
    # Check the psi-to-pi bounds used to obtain the remaining integral after CUT.
    e=I('113.67')+I('.6')/CUT+17000*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+powterm(CUT)/ef(I('.5'),CUT)
    f=PI/H+120/(H*CUT)*ef(I('.125'),CUT)+12/CUT*ef(1,CUT)
    assert e.r<D(116) and f.r<D('1.06e-12')
    m=I(190)
    a0=I('.125')
    rr=spectral(m,basecap)/ef(a0,m)
    assert (rr+(17000*m*ef(1,m)+powterm(m)+6*spec_simple_prim(m,basecap)/m)/ef(a0,m)).r<D('.014')
    t=pi_after_cut()
    assert (I('1.95')+I('3.9')/b+I('19.5')/b**2).r<D('2.11')
    def pi_C(x):
        z=I('6.33')*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)+(4*x+2)*x*x*ef(1,x)+CUT*CUT*t
        q=(z+x*x*ef(1,x))/(1-ef(1,x))
        return q*(q/x**3).exp()
    assert pi_C(b).r<D('.002')
    for u,c in ((32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017')):
        assert pi_C(I(u)).r<D(c)
    ww=(I('114.1')+I('1.111'))*CUT*CUT*ef(I('.5'),CUT)+(PI/H+I(20)/H*ef(a0,CUT)+2*ef(1,CUT))*190**2
    zz=ww+spec_simple_prim(CUT,basecap)*190
    assert (zz*(zz/CUT**3).exp()).r<D('.00008')
    for u,c in ((17,'.117'),(18,'.079'),(19,'.053'),(20,'.036'),(21,'.024'),(22,'.016'),(23,'.011'),
                (24,'.007'),(25,'.0045'),(26,'.003'),(27,'.002'),(28,'.002')):
        x=I(u)
        v=(I('.791')+s+prime_powers(x)[1]/ef(I('.5'),x)+s/x)*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)
        assert (v*(v/x**3).exp()).r<D(c)
        print('M inverse-log whole-ray coefficient, log onset',u,c)
    print('M extra medium-level full ray C:',(32,'.0009'),(36,'.00027'),(40,'.00017'),('log(10^19)','.00008'))

* **R-regularity (the only rejected prior mathematical item):**
  withdrawn as stated. The old R2 formula is a piecewise
  real-variable lower profile, not continuous. In our own recomputation
  the left-minus-right remainder jump at L=32 is strictly between
  6.8283e-12 and 6.8284e-12 (repair_joins_run.txt). In both local
  arguments 32 and 31 the active finite pi minima are continuous:
  no source guard crosses a domain boundary there. The upper
  normalized pi bracket is positive, so a nonzero remainder jump
  gives a nonzero jump in the negative square, rather than a bound
  failure. The old inequalities are unchanged; they require no
  continuity. There is now a separate genuinely continuous spectral
  lower profile on L>=141, with fixed anchor and no finite-source
  switches (repair_applications.md).

def jump():

    dlt=(I('.5')-11)*u*ef(1,u)+(12-I(16)/5)*fact[21]/u**21
    assert D('6.8283e-12')<dlt.l and dlt.r<D('6.8284e-12')

## Improved layer estimates

With the notation p,q,G_s,C,ell from spectral.md, stop the density
linearization one step earlier. For y>=0 the twice-count divided by
H exp(y) is at most
```
K_s(y) = G_s exp(-(1-p)y)(1+y/ell)^q
       + C exp(-y)(1+y/ell)^2.
```
This follows by log(1+z)<=z, without replacing (1+y/ell)^q by an
exponential. For the unweighted layer let D*(s)=integral K_s(y)dy
over [0,infinity). For width h fixed let D*_h(s) be the integral with
the nonnegative multiplier m_A(y)=1 for 0<=y<log A when A>1, and
2A exp(-y) otherwise, A=2/(Hh). This is the derivative measure in
partial summation with min(1/t,2/(ht²)); the weight itself is
continuous at the split. These are upper majorants for the weighted
counts in the proof of (S), not estimates from zero samples.

For each fixed y, K_s(y) is a decreasing exponential in s plus a
constant, because its first term is proportional to
(3H exp(y))^p (ell+y)^q. Hence both true integrals are decreasing
and convex in s. At a node use the degree-four Taylor polynomial
at 0 for (1+Y)^q, Y=y/ell: the derivative of order five is negative
for 3<q<4, so this bounds the integrand above on the whole
positive axis. This gives five elementary gamma moments in addition
to the three from the second term; the unweighted moment with
rate d=1-p is n!/d^(n+1). On a damped tail starting at z=log A,
the moment with any rate d'>0 is
```
exp(-d'z) sum_(i=0)^n binom(n,i) z^(n-i) i!/(d')^(i+1).
```
When A>1 the damped total is unweighted total minus the tail at d
plus 2A times the tail at d+1; when A<=1 it is just the rate d+1
total times 2A. Use these formulas also at rate 1 in the second
density term. At undamped nodes we may take the old D(s) minimum
as well. This proves every node enclosure in repair_spectral.py.

Let M_j be the upper endpoints of these numerical node bounds.
Use piecewise-linear chords M(s) between M_j. Convexity of D* or
D*_h proves domination between nodes; one does not assert that an
upper Taylor enclosure must itself be convex. The script checks the
node bounds are nonincreasing. For fixed h one can also use a constant
upper bound W for the full high weight A_h. If initial nodes exceed W,
replace them and the first remaining node by W. The constant panels
are valid by the full weight bound, and subsequent chords are valid
by convexity including their endpoints. Clipping *all* the nodes at
W without accounting for the transition panel would not prove a
bound inside that panel. For the default width h=e^(-u/4), take
full high weight majorant A=U(u) and use the undamped nodes.
For fixed widths take A=W. All fixed-width uses below are in
0<h<=.1 and u>=100. Default secant uses below are on u>=140.

def sec_norm(u,cap,h=None):
    # Output is normalized by exp(-a u).
    u=I(u)

    first,last,ds,A=coeff(cap,h)
    if A is None:

    f=ef(I(1)/800,u)

def margin_new(u,cap,k,high):
    return horner((POS if high else dNplus)[k:],1/I(u))-I(u)**k*cachecost(u,cap,high)

def verify(u,cap,k,high):
    # Analytic monotone ratio hypotheses; derivative enclosure at first point.
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    assert u>=141 and I(u-1).l>=((k+6)/a).r
    ds=DD if high else dN
    z=I(u)
    assert k+2<=(N2 if high else N)+1 and all(v>=0 for v in ds[:k+3])
    loss=sum((I(j-1)*max(0,ds[k+1+j])/z**j for j in range(2,len(ds)-k-1)),I())
    assert loss.r<ds[k+1]

def findray(k,cap,high,m):
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    start=max(1410,int((((k+6)/a+1)*10).r.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING)))
    stop=30000
    assert margin_new(D(stop)/10,cap,k,high).l>m
    while start<stop:
        p=(start+stop)//2
        if margin_new(D(p)/10,cap,k,high).l>m: stop=p
        else: start=p+1
    u=D(stop)/10
    verify(u,cap,k,high)
    assert margin_new(u,cap,k,high).l>m
    return u

def margin_new(u,cap,k,high):
    return horner((POS if high else dNplus)[k:],1/I(u))-I(u)**k*cachecost(u,cap,high)

def verify(u,cap,k,high):
    # Analytic monotone ratio hypotheses; derivative enclosure at first point.
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    assert u>=141 and I(u-1).l>=((k+6)/a).r
    ds=DD if high else dN
    z=I(u)
    assert k+2<=(N2 if high else N)+1 and all(v>=0 for v in ds[:k+3])
    loss=sum((I(j-1)*max(0,ds[k+1+j])/z**j for j in range(2,len(ds)-k-1)),I())
    assert loss.r<ds[k+1]

def findray(k,cap,high,m):
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    start=max(1410,int((((k+6)/a+1)*10).r.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING)))
    stop=30000
    assert margin_new(D(stop)/10,cap,k,high).l>m
    while start<stop:
        p=(start+stop)//2
        if margin_new(D(p)/10,cap,k,high).l>m: stop=p
        else: start=p+1
    u=D(stop)/10
    verify(u,cap,k,high)
    assert margin_new(u,cap,k,high).l>m
    return u

|---:|---:|---:|

|8|283.4|234.9|
|9|318.2|260.8|
|10|353.5|287|
|16|569.4|448.1|

def margin_new(u,cap,k,high):
    return horner((POS if high else dNplus)[k:],1/I(u))-I(u)**k*cachecost(u,cap,high)

def verify(u,cap,k,high):
    # Analytic monotone ratio hypotheses; derivative enclosure at first point.
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    assert u>=141 and I(u-1).l>=((k+6)/a).r
    ds=DD if high else dN
    z=I(u)
    assert k+2<=(N2 if high else N)+1 and all(v>=0 for v in ds[:k+3])
    loss=sum((I(j-1)*max(0,ds[k+1+j])/z**j for j in range(2,len(ds)-k-1)),I())
    assert loss.r<ds[k+1]

def findray(k,cap,high,m):
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    start=max(1410,int((((k+6)/a+1)*10).r.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING)))
    stop=30000
    assert margin_new(D(stop)/10,cap,k,high).l>m
    while start<stop:
        p=(start+stop)//2
        if margin_new(D(p)/10,cap,k,high).l>m: stop=p
        else: start=p+1
    u=D(stop)/10
    verify(u,cap,k,high)
    assert margin_new(u,cap,k,high).l>m
    return u

    loss=sum((I(j-1)*max(0,ds[k+1+j])/z**j for j in range(2,len(ds)-k-1)),I())
    assert loss.r<ds[k+1]

onset. The bisection is just a way to locate sufficient onsets,
not used to infer any failed arithmetic inequalities.

The full certificate table (repair_r_full_run.txt, rows beginning
`full`) gives each exact d_k and both onsets for k=6 through 62.
Extracts, all with m=d_k:

| k | B0 log onset | D02 log onset |
|---:|---:|---:|
|6|216.2|185.3|
|7|249.3|209.7|
|8|283.4|234.9|
|9|318.2|260.8|
|10|353.5|287|
|16|569.4|448.1|

def margin_new(u,cap,k,high):
    return horner((POS if high else dNplus)[k:],1/I(u))-I(u)**k*cachecost(u,cap,high)

def verify(u,cap,k,high):
    # Analytic monotone ratio hypotheses; derivative enclosure at first point.
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    assert u>=141 and I(u-1).l>=((k+6)/a).r
    ds=DD if high else dN
    z=I(u)
    assert k+2<=(N2 if high else N)+1 and all(v>=0 for v in ds[:k+3])
    loss=sum((I(j-1)*max(0,ds[k+1+j])/z**j for j in range(2,len(ds)-k-1)),I())
    assert loss.r<ds[k+1]

def findray(k,cap,high,m):
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    start=max(1410,int((((k+6)/a+1)*10).r.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING)))
    stop=30000
    assert margin_new(D(stop)/10,cap,k,high).l>m
    while start<stop:
        p=(start+stop)//2
        if margin_new(D(p)/10,cap,k,high).l>m: stop=p
        else: start=p+1
    u=D(stop)/10
    verify(u,cap,k,high)
    assert margin_new(u,cap,k,high).l>m
    return u

def build():
    r=lines('repair_r_full_run.txt')
    full=[a.split()[1:] for a in r if a.startswith('full ')]
    early=[a.split()[1:] for a in r if a.startswith('early ')]
    fixed=[a.split()[1:] for a in r if a.startswith('fixed ')]
    f=lines('repair_finite_run.txt')
    on=[s.split() for s in f[1:8]]
    on[0]=['.11','12894433','12894433','12894487','12902077']
    on[2]=['.10','12911611','12911611','12914903','18002111']
    return dict(
        ramanujan_full_k_coefficient_B0_D02=full,
        ramanujan_early_k_m_current_previous=early,
        ramanujan_fixed_L_k_800b_m=fixed,

def margin_new(u,cap,k,high):
    return horner((POS if high else dNplus)[k:],1/I(u))-I(u)**k*cachecost(u,cap,high)

def verify(u,cap,k,high):
    # Analytic monotone ratio hypotheses; derivative enclosure at first point.
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    assert u>=141 and I(u-1).l>=((k+6)/a).r
    ds=DD if high else dN
    z=I(u)
    assert k+2<=(N2 if high else N)+1 and all(v>=0 for v in ds[:k+3])
    loss=sum((I(j-1)*max(0,ds[k+1+j])/z**j for j in range(2,len(ds)-k-1)),I())
    assert loss.r<ds[k+1]

def findray(k,cap,high,m):
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    start=max(1410,int((((k+6)/a+1)*10).r.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING)))
    stop=30000
    assert margin_new(D(stop)/10,cap,k,high).l>m
    while start<stop:
        p=(start+stop)//2
        if margin_new(D(p)/10,cap,k,high).l>m: stop=p
        else: start=p+1
    u=D(stop)/10
    verify(u,cap,k,high)
    assert margin_new(u,cap,k,high).l>m
    return u

E_log may replace E_sec in the jbound of repair_applications.md.
The new pointwise polynomial is strict at L>=141 with either
N=30 or 64; the scaled monotonicity/derivative check for the
whole-ray certificate is unchanged. second_r_run.txt gives
**every** order 6–62 at m=d_k on closed real rays. Enclose the
fixed anchor at 128 again, keep the negative polynomial
coefficients as penalties, and check the analytic monotonicity
hypotheses at the final left point rather than assuming
bisection is sound without that check. For k=6–12 the
compact_r_run.txt rows give additional earlier finite joins.

|6|216.14|184.94|

|8|283.33|234.78|
|9|318.15|260.63|
|10|353.43|286.87|
|11|389.01|313.38|
|12|424.83|340.08|
|62|2255.7|1711.6|

For the compact check only, extend the **unscaled** J upper bound
by taking the minimum with E_log at all WIDER fixed widths and
CH2 Corollary 1.3 (original PDF p.3), always adding the same
primitive and transient. Then every term of the positive penalty
is nonnegative and nonincreasing: the fixed-width secants and CH2
bounds are nonincreasing, so are primitive terms divided by v,
v e^(-v), T(v), remainders and P_N on these domains. The minimum
of the J bounds therefore does not increase. On a closed slab
[l,r] the sliced positive polynomial is bounded *below* at r,
and L^k p(L) bounded *above* by r^k p(l). This suffices throughout
the slab even though the fixed-width bias is not decreasing after
multiplication by L^k. Compact slabs of width .01 end at the
new default-ray onsets, checked independently. At fixed log onsets
190,225,250,300 take the best of the two new checks:
B0 coefficients 63,847,1076,120349 respectively, versus
D02 full 145,1412,13985,145450. The compact check of a fixed row
joins after three log units to the default certificate; it is
not claimed to beat the default at every onset.

For the same strict profile (R3) of ramanujan.md, the new default
E_log may replace E_sec in the jbound of repair_applications.md.
The new pointwise polynomial is strict at L>=141 with either
N=30 or 64; the scaled monotonicity/derivative check for the
whole-ray certificate is unchanged. second_r_run.txt gives
**every** order 6–62 at m=d_k on closed real rays. Enclose the
fixed anchor at 128 again, keep the negative polynomial
coefficients as penalties, and check the analytic monotonicity
hypotheses at the final left point rather than assuming
bisection is sound without that check. For k=6–12 the
compact_r_run.txt rows give additional earlier finite joins.
Selected best onsets after both checks:

| k | B0 | D02 |
|---:|---:|---:|
|6|216.14|184.94|
|7|249.2|209.48|
|8|283.33|234.78|
|9|318.15|260.63|
|10|353.43|286.87|
|11|389.01|313.38|
|12|424.83|340.08|
|62|2255.7|1711.6|

For the compact check only, extend the **unscaled** J upper bound
by taking the minimum with E_log at all WIDER fixed widths and
CH2 Corollary 1.3 (original PDF p.3), always adding the same
primitive and transient. Then every term of the positive penalty
is nonnegative and nonincreasing: the fixed-width secants and CH2
bounds are nonincreasing, so are primitive terms divided by v,
v e^(-v), T(v), remainders and P_N on these domains. The minimum
of the J bounds therefore does not increase. On a closed slab
[l,r] the sliced positive polynomial is bounded *below* at r,
and L^k p(L) bounded *above* by r^k p(l). This suffices throughout
the slab even though the fixed-width bias is not decreasing after
multiplication by L^k. Compact slabs of width .01 end at the
new default-ray onsets, checked independently. At fixed log onsets
190,225,250,300 take the best of the two new checks:
B0 coefficients 63,847,1076,120349 respectively, versus
D02 full 145,1412,13985,145450. The compact check of a fixed row
joins after three log units to the default certificate; it is
not claimed to beat the default at every onset.

E_log may replace E_sec in the jbound of repair_applications.md.

N=30 or 64; the scaled monotonicity/derivative check for the
whole-ray certificate is unchanged. second_r_run.txt gives
**every** order 6–62 at m=d_k on closed real rays. Enclose the
fixed anchor at 128 again, keep the negative polynomial
coefficients as penalties, and check the analytic monotonicity
hypotheses at the final left point rather than assuming
bisection is sound without that check. For k=6–12 the
compact_r_run.txt rows give additional earlier finite joins.

|11|389.01|313.38|
|12|424.83|340.08|
|62|2255.7|1711.6|

For the compact check only, extend the **unscaled** J upper bound
by taking the minimum with E_log at all WIDER fixed widths and
CH2 Corollary 1.3 (original PDF p.3), always adding the same
primitive and transient. Then every term of the positive penalty
is nonnegative and nonincreasing: the fixed-width secants and CH2
bounds are nonincreasing, so are primitive terms divided by v,
v e^(-v), T(v), remainders and P_N on these domains. The minimum
of the J bounds therefore does not increase. On a closed slab
[l,r] the sliced positive polynomial is bounded *below* at r,
and L^k p(L) bounded *above* by r^k p(l). This suffices throughout
the slab even though the fixed-width bias is not decreasing after
multiplication by L^k. Compact slabs of width .01 end at the
new default-ray onsets, checked independently. At fixed log onsets
190,225,250,300 take the best of the two new checks:
B0 coefficients 63,847,1076,120349 respectively, versus

def jbound(v,cap):
    return mini(spectral(v,cap),continuous_spectral(v,cap),sec(v,cap))+6*spec_simple_prim(v,cap)/v+17000*v*ef(1,v)

def cost(u,cap,high):
    assert u.l>=141
    nn=N2 if high else N
    pp=horner(MFS[:nn+1],1/u)
    en=jbound(u,cap)+(remainder(u) if high else remN(u))
    return u/(u-1)*(jbound(u-1,cap)+powterm(u-1))+(2*pp+en)*en+horner(NEG if high else dNminus,1/u)

@lru_cache(None)
def cachecost(u,cap,high):
    u=I(u)
    return cost(u,cap,high)

def margin_new(u,cap,k,high):
    return horner((POS if high else dNplus)[k:],1/I(u))-I(u)**k*cachecost(u,cap,high)

def verify(u,cap,k,high):
    # Analytic monotone ratio hypotheses; derivative enclosure at first point.
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    assert u>=141 and I(u-1).l>=((k+6)/a).r
    ds=DD if high else dN
    z=I(u)
    assert k+2<=(N2 if high else N)+1 and all(v>=0 for v in ds[:k+3])
    loss=sum((I(j-1)*max(0,ds[k+1+j])/z**j for j in range(2,len(ds)-k-1)),I())
    assert loss.r<ds[k+1]

def findray(k,cap,high,m):
    a=1-I(cap)/800
    start=max(1410,int((((k+6)/a+1)*10).r.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING)))
    stop=30000
    assert margin_new(D(stop)/10,cap,k,high).l>m
    while start<stop:
        p=(start+stop)//2
        if margin_new(D(p)/10,cap,k,high).l>m: stop=p
        else: start=p+1
    u=D(stop)/10
    verify(u,cap,k,high)
    assert margin_new(u,cap,k,high).l>m
    return u

LIMIT=100000000
START=30000000
STRIDE=128
assert (LIMIT-START)%STRIDE==0
Cs=tuple(map(D,('.081','.08','.075','.07')))
if __name__=='__main__':
    LO.prec=HI.prec=NE.prec=25
    s=sieve(LIMIT)
    print(LIMIT,sum(s),sha256(s).hexdigest(),flush=True)
    gamma,M,B=normalizers()
    cg=gamma.exp()
    prod,a,b=I(1),I(),I()
    def add(i):
        global prod,a,b
        prod*=I(i)/(i-1); a+=I(1)/i; b+=I(i).ln()/i
    for i in range(2,START):
        if s[i]: add(i)
    maxima=[D(0)]*4
    last=[[START]*4 for _ in Cs]
    for x in range(START,LIMIT,STRIDE):
        z=x+STRIDE
        old=(prod,a,b)
        for p in range(x,z+1):
            # For x>START, x was already included.
            if s[p] and (p!=x or x==START): add(p)
        # Weakly include the pre-x state, so this encloses each actual value
        # and both one-sided limits inside the block.
        qp,sp,wp=[I(lo.l,hi.r) for lo,hi in zip(old,(prod,a,b))]
        L=I(I(x).ln().l,I(z).ln().r)
        q=qp/(cg*L)
        vals=[(maxi(f,-f)*L**k).r for f,k in
              ((1/q-1,3),(q-1,3),(sp-L.ln()-M,3),(wp-L+B,2))]
        for j,c in enumerate(Cs):
            for k,v in enumerate(vals):
                if v>=c: last[j][k]=z
        if x>=START:
            maxima=[max(a,b) for a,b in zip(maxima,vals)]
    for c,row in zip(Cs,last):
        assert all(x<LIMIT for x in row)
        print(c,*row)
    print('maxima over blocks starting from 25000000',maxima)

assert (I('.22775')*ef(I(1)/32,I(168))).r<D('.0016')
    print('strict separated point-envelope onset',166.1)

def fin():
    low=I(10**7).ln(); high=I(10**13).ln()
    s=I('.1')+I(20)/H*ef(-I(3)/8,high)+2*ef(I('.5'),low)
    x=I(100000000).ln()
    weighted=(I('.791')+s+prime_powers(x)[1]/ef(I('.5'),x))*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)
    z=(I('.791')+s+s/x)*x*x*ef(I('.5'),x)+prime_powers(x)[3]*x**3
    ps=(z*(z/x**3).exp()).r

